newsitem.title: USA: Enron sees EPS growth of 15 pct/year.
newsitem.headline: Enron sees EPS growth of 15 pct/year.

text.p: Enron Corp earnings per share will double by the year 2000 with annual growth of 15 percent, cheif executive Kenneth Lay said Wednesday.
"Our aim is double digit growth every year to 2000," he told the PaineWebber annual energy conference. The company earned 2.31 per share last year.
Lay said non-recurring items would make no more than 10 percent of net income by 2000.
He said wholesale electricity volumes in the first quarter of this year would be equivalent to half of the total for all of 1996.
In 1996, Enron sold 60.15 million megawatt hours of power.
"We will become the largest wholesale marketer of electricity in the U.S. We also aim to overtake Southern Co as the largest maketer of all," Lay said.
He said Enron is aiming for a 10 to 20 percent share of the $200 billion electricity retail market by 20001.
"Using a one to two percent margin, we will be generating $200 million to $400 million of after tax net income within five years," from this market Lay said.
